SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.66
EXPLANATION: The clear Raman band at 1715 cm⁻¹ indicates a saturated carbonyl (GFQ-011), consistent with an aliphatic ketone. Strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2909/2941 cm⁻¹ and CH₂ scissoring at 1458 cm⁻¹ fit an n-alkyl chain (GFQ-003). Absence of aldehydic C–H bands near 2720–2830 cm⁻¹ argues against aldehydes or formate esters, and the ester ν(C=O) typically appears higher (~1735–1750 cm⁻¹) with a strong ν(C–O) near 1180–1250 cm⁻¹, which is not evident. The remaining bands at 1108/1045/834/750 cm⁻¹ are compatible with skeletal C–C/C–C–C modes of an aliphatic ketone. Among candidates, 3-heptanone (index 2) best matches these features.
